Probate-Sisco

Preserved Primary Document • probt-s4.htm

In the name of God, Amen. I George Sisco being sick and in a low state of health but in perfect reason of mind do make this my last will and testament. I give and bequeath to my Sister Emila Hanser two cows and loom and all the rest and the Remainder of my Household goods. I give and bequeath to my Brother William Sisco and Sister Emela Hanser all the rest of my Estate to be equal divided between the two. I do give my Brother William Sisco my hole and Soul Executor this being my last will and testament where unto I have Set my hand this tenth day of November in the Year of our Lord one thousand Eight Hundred and fourteen----1814. Signed in the presents of us. Luke Richards George Comerford Miller Richard George Sisco signed with his own somewhat shaky hand. Be it remembered that on the twenty sixth day of November in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and fourteen, Letters of Administration of the Estate of said George Sisco dec'd were granted in due form of Law granted unto William Sisco Executor in said will named being sworn gave bond with Abraham Allee his surety in the sum of one thousand dollars lawful money and on the said twenty sixth day of November in the year aforesaid the last will and testament of said George Sisco was proved and approved. 26 November, 1814 Testamentary Bond recorded in Book P, folio 69 William Sisco, Executor of the estate of George Sisco, and Abraham Allee posted bond guaranteeing the inventory on William's estate to be filed before 26 May, 1815. 2 December, 1814 Inventory of George Sisco Wearing Apparel ($8) 1 chest, 1 trunk and (unclear) linnens ($6.83) 3 windsor chairs, 2 small cupboards, 3 small old desks (5.75) 1 pair Steelyards, 1 teakettle, 1 Iron Pot (4-) 1 Quill wheel 24 lbs. old feathers 2 cows ($39) 1 Loom & tackling 1 warping mill (26.50) 1 large Steel trap and chain ($2) Total: $92.08 Testamentary Account George Francisco 22 November, 1815 To James Harper Register of Kent County, William Sisco, Executor of the last will and Testament of George Francisco dec'd Presents the following Testamentary Account of the Estate of said deceased for adjustment. Probate-Sisco
Preserved Primary Document • probt-s4.htm




In the name of God, Amen. I George Sisco  being sick and in a low state of health but in perfect reason of mind do make this my last will and testament. I give and bequeath to my Sister Emila Hanser two cows and loom and all the rest and the Remainder of my Household goods. 

I give and bequeath to my Brother William Sisco and Sister Emela Hanser all the rest of my Estate to be equal divided between the two.  I do give my Brother William Sisco my hole and Soul Executor this being my last will and testament where unto I have Set my hand this tenth day of November in the Year of our Lord one thousand Eight Hundred and fourteen----
1814
. 
Signed in the presents of us. 
Luke Richards 
George Comerford 
Miller Richard 

George Sisco signed with his own somewhat shaky hand. 



Be it remembered that on the twenty sixth day of November in the year of our Lord one thousand eight hundred and fourteen, Letters of Administration of the Estate of said George Sisco dec'd were granted in due form of Law granted unto William Sisco Executor in said will named being sworn gave bond with Abraham Allee his surety in the sum of one thousand dollars lawful money and on the said twenty sixth day of November in the year aforesaid the last will and testament of said George Sisco was proved and approved. 



 26 November, 
1814
 Testamentary Bond  
recorded in Book P, folio 69 
William Sisco, Executor of the estate of George Sisco, and Abraham Allee posted bond guaranteeing the inventory on William's estate to be filed before 26 May, 
1815
. 
 



 2 December, 
1814
